summary: Current Adobe Reader 26.002.22031 (64-bit) on Windows 11 renders all 43 pages of the five PDFs without error dialogs; copied text identical to default on all 28 candidate pages; 33/33 candidate searches return the same instance counts and hits as default; default-vs-candidate differences in Reader track the same differences in pinned PDFium (ratio 0.90-1.11), and candidates are no further from PDFium than default is.

method.per_page: fresh Reader launch with /A open parameters; maximised; Fit Page (Ctrl+0) full-screen capture; click canvas, Ctrl+A/Ctrl+C, clipboard saved as UTF-8; relaunch at zoom=400 on the densest text window (crops.json; mixed p2 fixed on the title and the member-518 "with" line); top-level window classes recorded after every open
method.search: per PDF, 11 words via /A search=<word>; Search window brought forward and captured; instance count and hit list compared with default
method.pdfium_control: pinned PDFium chromium/8100 (sha256 b8784cbd...539e) rendered at the Reader fit scale (canvas height / page height), registered by integer-offset search; compare default-vs-candidate difference within Reader with the same difference within PDFium, and Reader-vs-PDFium distance for candidate against the same distance for default
method.mask: Reader "Reopen closed PDFs" notice (screen x>=1540, y<220), caused by force-closing Reader between captures, masked out of pixel metrics

search.hit_list_note: the 11 non-identical hit lists differ only in UI state (first-row selection colour grey vs blue, file-name row); hit text identical

fit_render.interpretation: Reader shows exactly the substitution-driven differences PDFium shows, and no extra; no candidate is further from PDFium than default

results.zoom400: visually inspected: substitutions appear as faint outline-edge differences only; no missing glyphs, wrong component offsets or misplaced glyphs; member 518 "with" renders normally
results.incidental_default_defect: mixed p2 default renders the e of "the professional" as a small raised e; cover-2.0 renders it normally (consistent with PDFium)
